title: Base change of finite locally free groupoid quotient stacks
statement: Work over a field $k$ [def-weil-field], with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and the $2$-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Representable means representable by algebraic spaces. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. For a groupoid scheme $(P,Q,s,t,e,i,c)$ [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws], write $[P/Q]$ for the fppf stackification [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] of the groupoid with objects $P(T)$ and arrows $Q(T)$ on every test scheme $T$. Assume $s,t:Q\to P$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. For any map $P\to B$ to an algebraic space that is invariant under $Q$ (its composites with $s$ and $t$ agree), and any algebraic-space map $B'\to B$, quotient formation commutes with this base change: $[P_{B'}/Q_{B'}]\simeq[P/Q]\times_B B'$. The base-changed objects $P_{B'},Q_{B'}$ may be algebraic spaces; their quotient means the fppf stackification of their groupoid of test-scheme points, by the same definition.

source.place: Tag 0DTG (lemma-base-change-quotient-stack), for a groupoid with finite locally free source and target.

proof.text: Regard the $k$-schemes $P,Q$ as their actual representable fppf sheaves, hence as algebraic spaces, by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. This retains $P(T),Q(T)$ and all their structure maps on every test scheme. Thus the functorial groupoid laws of [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws] give the same groupoid in algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Write $a:P\to B$. The given equality $as=at$ is exactly invariance of $a$. On test schemes the base-changed objects are pairs $(p,b')$ and $(q,b')$ with $a(p)=g(b')$ and $as(q)=g(b')$ respectively; all groupoid operations retain the second coordinate. The source, target, unit, inverse and composition laws therefore remain the original laws in the first coordinate. These are precisely the base changes appearing in the existing invariant-base-change theorem.

source.place: Tag 0DTG (lemma-base-change-quotient-stack), hypotheses; scheme-as-space convention of Tags 025Y and 03G1 in def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-quotient-stack-invariant-base-change] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $(U,R)=(P,Q)$, $X=B$ and $X_1=B'$. Step 1 verifies its groupoid and invariance hypotheses; $B,B'$ and $g:B'\to B$ are the algebraic spaces and map required there. Its quotient notation is the fppf stackification of the same test-scheme groupoids used in this statement, including when $P_{B'}$ and $Q_{B'}$ are only algebraic spaces. The resulting 2-cartesian square has top row $[P_{B'}/Q_{B'}]\to[P/Q]$ and bottom row $B'\to B$, so its universal comparison is exactly $[P_{B'}/Q_{B'}]\simeq[P/Q]\times_B B'$. The cited theorem has no finiteness or flatness hypothesis, so the assumed finite local freeness of $s,t$ imposes no additional verification for this application.
